HowTo.Title: How to use
HowTo.Step1Text: At the top of the Routes page. The route list comes live from Steam.
HowTo.Step3Text: Click Allowed on a route to block it, use Auto select, or pick a preset.
HowTo.Step4Text: Start or restart matchmaking. Blocked locations aren't used anymore.
HowTo.FaqVac: Can I get VAC banned for using it?
HowTo.FaqVacAnswer: Steam Route Tool never touches the game: it doesn't read or change game files or memory and doesn't inject anything. It only adds Windows Firewall rules that stop your PC from connecting to the relay servers you picked, the same as blocking them by hand in Windows Defender Firewall. VAC looks for cheats that modify the game, and firewall-based server pickers like this one have been used for years without known bans. Only Valve can guarantee anything, though, so use it at your own discretion.
HowTo.FaqAdmin: Why does it need administrator rights?
HowTo.FaqAdminAnswer: Windows only lets administrators add or remove firewall rules. The tool uses those rights for its own rules (named SteamRouteTool-…) and nothing else. It's open source, so you can check what it does on GitHub.
HowTo.FaqLowerPingAnswer: Not directly: it can't make a connection faster. It stops matchmaking from putting you on distant or unwanted servers, so you end up on the closest ones you allowed. Ping to a server you can still reach stays the same.
HowTo.FaqQueue: Why do I wait longer for a match, or can't find one?
HowTo.FaqQueueAnswer: Fewer allowed locations mean fewer servers to match on, especially at night or in a small region. Keep a few nearby routes open, or unblock more if the queue takes too long. With every route blocked, you can't connect at all.
HowTo.FaqModes: Which games and modes does it affect?
HowTo.FaqModesAnswer: Everything that connects through Valve's relays: official matchmaking in Counter-Strike 2 (Premier, Competitive, Casual, Deathmatch and more), Dota 2 and Deadlock. Third-party platforms like FACEIT and community servers you join by IP use their own servers and aren't affected. Other Steam games that use Valve's relay network can be affected too, since the rules apply to the whole PC.
HowTo.FaqPrivacyAnswer: No. It only connects to Steam to get the route list, to GitHub to check for updates, and to the relays to ping them. Your settings stay on your PC.
HowTo.WhatItDoes1: Valve games like Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2 and Deadlock connect you to game servers through Valve's relay network (Steam Datagram Relay). Steam Route Tool lets you block relays in specific locations with Windows Firewall, so matchmaking only puts you on the servers you want, for example only nearby ones.
HowTo.WhenDone: When you're done, use **Unblock all** in the ⋯ menu to remove every rule, or leave them: they stay until you change them. To block only while the app is open, turn on **Unblock all routes when closing** in Settings.
HowTo.Blocking1: Click the region's chip (for example Europe) above the list, then choose **Block all except shown** in the ⋯ menu. Every other route is blocked and the shown ones are allowed. This works with the search box too.
HowTo.Blocking2: In the **Auto select** card, set how many routes to keep with − and +, then click **Apply**: the fastest ones stay allowed and all others are blocked. Hover **Apply** for a preview, and use **Undo** in the confirmation if you change your mind. It uses each route's best known ping; blocked routes can't be pinged, so for them the last measured ping is used. For the most accurate result, use **Unblock all** (⋯ menu) and **Ping all** first.
HowTo.Blocking3: Most locations have several relay servers. Click the arrow next to a route to show them and block single relays. A route with only some relays blocked shows **Partly**.
HowTo.Blocking4: Use the sort list next to the search box to sort by region, name, ping or status. Filter with the search box, the region chips and **All / Blocked / Not blocked**, or turn off **Group by region** in the ⋯ menu for one flat list.
HowTo.Presets1: A preset is a named set of blocked routes, for example "EU blocked" or "Warsaw only". Block the routes you want, click **Save current** under **Presets** on the Routes page, type a name and click **Save**. Each game has its own presets.
HowTo.Presets2: Click a preset's chip to block exactly its routes and allow all others; **Undo** brings back what was blocked before. The chip of the preset that matches what's blocked now is highlighted; none is once you change something. You can also switch presets from the tray icon's menu.
HowTo.Presets3: To update a preset, block the routes you want and save again under its name. Rename a preset by editing its name in the same panel, or delete it with the bin button. A route saved as fully blocked stays fully blocked even if Valve adds relays to it later.
HowTo.AutoPreset: Apply a preset when a game starts
HowTo.AutoPresetText: Open **Save current** on the Routes page and choose a preset under **Apply when the game starts**. While Steam Route Tool runs (for example in the tray), it notices when that game starts, switches to it and applies the preset. Each game has its own choice; **Don't apply a preset** turns it off.
HowTo.Profiles1: Each game remembers its own blocked routes. When you switch games, that game's saved selection is applied to the firewall automatically.
HowTo.Profiles2: Valve's games share the same relay servers, and firewall rules apply to your whole PC. Blocking a route for one game therefore blocks it for every game until you switch profiles or unblock it.
HowTo.Pings1: Greyed values are from your last session and are replaced as fresh results arrive. A collapsed route shows the best ping of its relays. **no reply** means none of the tried relays answered; **blocked** routes aren't pinged because their pings are blocked too. Click any ping to measure it again.
HowTo.Pings2: Pings are sent quickly in a first round and anything that didn't answer is retried one at a time. Some routers (flood protection) and ISPs drop replies when many pings are sent at once; on such networks the list fills in over 10–20 seconds.
HowTo.Background1: Turn on **Minimize to tray** in Settings to keep the app out of the taskbar: minimizing hides the window and leaves an icon in the notification area (on Windows 10 it may be behind the ^ arrow; drag it onto the taskbar to keep it visible). Click the icon to open the window, or right-click it to switch games and presets, run Auto select, unblock all routes or exit.
HowTo.Background2: Turn on **Start with Windows** to start the app minimized when you sign in. This is useful together with **Unblock all routes when closing**, which only blocks routes while the app is running. Starting the app again while it's already running brings back the open window.
HowTo.Background3: With **Close to tray** (on by default), the close button also keeps the app running in the tray. Exit from the tray icon's menu.
HowTo.ShortcutsText: **Ctrl+F** search the routes, **F5** ping all routes, **Ctrl+1**, **Ctrl+2** and **Ctrl+3** switch to Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2 and Deadlock. They work from every page.
HowTo.Troubleshooting1: The tool needs administrator rights (Windows asks when it starts) and the Windows Defender Firewall service must be running. Third-party firewalls that replace Windows Firewall aren't supported.
HowTo.FaqStillConnected: Still connected to a blocked location
HowTo.Troubleshooting2: Blocking only affects new connections. Leave the match and search again.
HowTo.Troubleshooting3: Open Windows Defender Firewall (Settings → Open Windows Firewall) → Outbound Rules. The rules are named SteamRouteTool-UDP/TCP/ICMP-<route> and grouped under SteamRouteTool.
HowTo.Troubleshooting4: The download isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn the first time. Choose More info, then Run anyway.
HowTo.Removing1: Use **Unblock all** in the ⋯ menu first, so no firewall rules are left behind, and turn off **Start with Windows** in Settings. Then delete the program and, if you like, its settings folder:
